title: Configure and verify Layer 2 discovery protocols

questions.question: Which protocol is an IEEE standard that collects information from neighboring devices on their identity and capabilities?
questions.explanation: LLDP is IEEE 802.1AB and provides standards-based neighbor discovery.

correct.explanation: LLDP (IEEE 802.1AB) is the vendor-neutral neighbor discovery standard — CDP is Cisco-proprietary.

incorrect.explanation: CDP is Cisco-only — the stem asks for the IEEE standard → LLDP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Cisco CDP on IEEE question
incorrect.whatItDoes: CDP points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for LLDP is IEEE 802.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "LLDP is IEEE 802", LLDP satisfies what this question tests — CDP does not.

incorrect.explanation: 802.1b is not the LLDP standard — use 802.1AB (LLDP).
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Wrong 802.1 letter
incorrect.whatItDoes: 802.1b points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for LLDP is IEEE 802.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "LLDP is IEEE 802", LLDP satisfies what this question tests — 802.1b does not.

incorrect.explanation: 802.1a is unrelated — neighbor discovery IEEE standard is LLDP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Invented 802.1 variant
incorrect.whatItDoes: 802.1a points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for LLDP is IEEE 802.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "LLDP is IEEE 802", LLDP satisfies what this question tests — 802.1a does not.

answerReview.examTip: Multi-vendor neighbor discovery → LLDP. Cisco-only → CDP.

questions.question: You want to turn off CDP on a switch. Which command would you enter?
questions.explanation: no cdp run disables CDP globally.

correct.explanation: no cdp run disables CDP globally.

incorrect.explanation: cdp disable is not valid IOS syntax — the global command to turn off CDP on the entire switch is no cdp run in global configuration mode.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using invalid cdp disable global command
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#cdp disable points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for no cdp run disables CDP globally.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "no cdp run disables CDP globally", Switch(config-if)#no cdp run satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#cdp disable does not.

incorrect.explanation: no cdp enable under an interface disables CDP on that port only — the stem asks to turn off CDP on the whole switch, which requires global no cdp run.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using per-interface disable for global CDP off
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-if)#no cdp enable points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for no cdp run disables CDP globally.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "no cdp run disables CDP globally", Switch(config-if)#no cdp run satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-if)#no cdp enable does not.

incorrect.explanation: no cdp alone is incomplete IOS syntax — the recognized global command is no cdp run to disable CDP switch-wide.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using incomplete no cdp without run keyword
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#no cdp points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for no cdp run disables CDP globally.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "no cdp run disables CDP globally", Switch(config-if)#no cdp run satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#no cdp does not.

answerReview.examTip: Disable CDP globally → no cdp run. Per-port → no cdp enable on interface.

questions.question: How often are CDP frames sent out of the device by default?
questions.explanation: CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default.

correct.explanation: CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default.

incorrect.explanation: CDP default timer is 60 seconds, not 30 — advertisements are sent once per minute unless changed with cdp timer.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing 30-second interval with CDP default
incorrect.whatItDoes: Every 30 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default", Every 60 seconds satisfies what this question tests — Every 30 seconds does not.

incorrect.explanation: 90 seconds is not the default CDP advertisement interval — IOS sends CDP updates every 60 seconds by default.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting 90 seconds as CDP timer default
incorrect.whatItDoes: Every 90 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default", Every 60 seconds satisfies what this question tests — Every 90 seconds does not.

incorrect.explanation: 180 seconds is the default CDP hold-time, not the advertisement interval — frames are sent every 60 seconds, and neighbors are held for 180 seconds of silence.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing CDP hold-time (180 s) with timer (60 s)
incorrect.whatItDoes: Every 180 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default", Every 60 seconds satisfies what this question tests — Every 180 seconds does not.

answerReview.examTip: CDP defaults: timer 60 s, hold-time 180 s — do not swap them.

questions.question: What is the default value of the CDP holddown timer for CDP entries?

incorrect.explanation: 30 seconds is not the default CDP hold-time — IOS keeps neighbor entries for 180 seconds without updates before removing them.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Underestimating default CDP hold-time
incorrect.whatItDoes: 30 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: MAC aging (CDP holdtime defaults to 180 seconds): 180 seconds is the default or configured timer — 30 seconds states the wrong timeout value or behavior.

incorrect.explanation: 60 seconds is the default CDP advertisement timer, not the hold-time — entries persist for 180 seconds (three missed advertisements) before aging out.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using advertisement timer as hold-time default
incorrect.whatItDoes: 60 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: MAC aging (CDP holdtime defaults to 180 seconds): 180 seconds is the default or configured timer — 60 seconds states the wrong timeout value or behavior.

incorrect.explanation: 90 seconds is not the default CDP hold-time — the factory default is 180 seconds, three times the 60-second advertisement interval.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting 90 s as CDP hold-time default
incorrect.whatItDoes: 90 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: MAC aging (CDP holdtime defaults to 180 seconds): 180 seconds is the default or configured timer — 90 seconds states the wrong timeout value or behavior.

answerReview.examTip: CDP hold-time default = 180 s (3× the 60 s advertisement timer).

questions.question: You have several non-Cisco IP phones and you want to allow automatic power adjustments on the Cisco Power over an Ethernet (PoE) switch. Which command will allow you to achieve this?
questions.explanation: lldp run enables LLDP globally, including LLDP-MED capabilities.

correct.explanation: LLDP-MED for non-Cisco phones requires global lldp run from configuration mode so the switch can negotiate power and capabilities.

incorrect.explanation: Global configuration uses (config)# — Switch#lldp run is not valid privileged-exec syntax for enabling LLDP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Running lldp run from privileged exec instead of config mode
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#lldp run points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for lldp run enables LLDP globally, including LLDP-MED capabilities.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "lldp run enables LLDP globally, including LLDP-MED capabilities", Switch(config)#lldp run satisfies what this question tests — Switch#lldp run does not.

incorrect.explanation: lldp enable is not the standard global IOS command — use lldp run in configuration mode.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Substituting lldp enable for lldp run
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#lldp enable points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for lldp run enables LLDP globally, including LLDP-MED capabilities.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "lldp run enables LLDP globally, including LLDP-MED capabilities", Switch(config)#lldp run satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#lldp enable does not.

incorrect.explanation: LLDP must be configured from global configuration mode — privileged exec # prompt cannot enable lldp run.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Attempting global LLDP enable from exec mode
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#lldp enable points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for lldp run enables LLDP globally, including LLDP-MED capabilities.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "lldp run enables LLDP globally, including LLDP-MED capabilities", Switch(config)#lldp run satisfies what this question tests — Switch#lldp enable does not.

answerReview.examTip: PoE + multivendor phones → lldp run globally for LLDP-MED power negotiation.

questions.question: Which command will allow you to see LLDP devices connected to a switch?
questions.explanation: show lldp neighbor detail shows detailed LLDP neighbor information.

incorrect.explanation: show lldp alone is incomplete syntax on many platforms — neighbor detail is the standard verification command.

incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#show lldp points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for show lldp neighbor detail shows detailed LLDP neighbor information.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "show lldp neighbor detail shows detailed LLDP neighbor information", Switch#show lldp neighbor detail satisfies what this question tests — Switch#show lldp does not.

incorrect.explanation: show lldp devices is not standard IOS — use show lldp neighbors or show lldp neighbor detail.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Inventing show lldp devices command
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#show lldp devices points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for show lldp neighbor detail shows detailed LLDP neighbor information.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "show lldp neighbor detail shows detailed LLDP neighbor information", Switch#show lldp neighbor detail satisfies what this question tests — Switch#show lldp devices does not.

questions.question: What is the default LLDP advertisement interval?
questions.explanation: LLDP advertises every 30 seconds by default.

correct.explanation: LLDP sends neighbor advertisements every 30 seconds by default — faster than CDP's 60-second interval.

incorrect.explanation: 60 seconds is the default CDP advertisement interval — LLDP defaults to 30 seconds.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Applying CDP 60 s default to LLDP
incorrect.whatItDoes: 60 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "LLDP advertises every 30 seconds by default", 30 seconds satisfies what this question tests — 60 seconds does not.

incorrect.explanation: 90 seconds is not the LLDP default advertisement timer — stock IOS uses 30 seconds.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting tripled LLDP interval
incorrect.whatItDoes: 90 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "LLDP advertises every 30 seconds by default", 30 seconds satisfies what this question tests — 90 seconds does not.

incorrect.explanation: 120 seconds is the LLDP holdtime default, not the transmit interval — advertisements go out every 30 s.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing LLDP holdtime with advertisement interval
incorrect.whatItDoes: 120 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "LLDP advertises every 30 seconds by default", 30 seconds satisfies what this question tests — 120 seconds does not.

answerReview.examTip: LLDP timers: TX every 30 s; holdtime 120 s — do not swap with CDP 60/180.

questions.question: You want to disable LLDP from sending advertisements on a single interface. Which command will you use?

incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "no lldp transmit suppresses outgoing LLDP on an interface", Switch(config-if)#no lldp transmit satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-if)#no lldp does not.

incorrect.explanation: no lldp receive blocks inbound LLDP processing — the stem asks to stop sending advertisements outbound.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Disabling receive when transmit must be stopped
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-if)#no lldp receive points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for no lldp transmit suppresses outgoing LLDP on an interface.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "no lldp transmit suppresses outgoing LLDP on an interface", Switch(config-if)#no lldp transmit satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-if)#no lldp receive does not.

incorrect.explanation: no lldp enable is not standard IOS interface syntax — use no lldp transmit to stop outbound ads.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Inventing no lldp enable interface command
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-if)#no lldp enable points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for no lldp transmit suppresses outgoing LLDP on an interface.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "no lldp transmit suppresses outgoing LLDP on an interface", Switch(config-if)#no lldp transmit satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-if)#no lldp enable does not.

incorrect.explanation: 30 seconds is the LLDP advertisement interval — holdtime before aging a neighbor is 120 seconds.

incorrect.whatItDoes: 30 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: MAC aging (LLDP holdtime defaults to 120 seconds): 120 seconds is the default or configured timer — 30 seconds states the wrong timeout value or behavior.

incorrect.explanation: 60 seconds is CDP's advertisement default — LLDP holdtime is 120 seconds.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using CDP timer for LLDP holdtime
incorrect.whatItDoes: 60 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: MAC aging (LLDP holdtime defaults to 120 seconds): 120 seconds is the default or configured timer — 60 seconds states the wrong timeout value or behavior.

incorrect.explanation: 90 seconds is not the LLDP holdtime default — Cisco IOS uses 120 seconds for neighbor entry aging.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting non-default LLDP holdtime value
incorrect.whatItDoes: 90 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.

questions.question:
CDP neighbor detail (SwitchB):
Device ID: SwitchB
Entry address(es): IP 192.168.1.2
Platform: cisco WS-C2960, Capabilities: Switch
Interface: GigabitEthernet0/2, Port ID (outgoing port): GigabitEthernet0/1
Holdtime: 162 sec

The following output shows the output of the CDP details. Which statement is correct about what is displayed?
choices: The advertisement was seen 162 seconds ago.
Switch B interface Gi0/1 connects to Switch A.
Switch B interface Gi0/2 connects to Switch A.
The IP address of Switch B is 192.168.1.1.
questions.explanation: CDP detail output identifies the local and remote interfaces, holdtime, and management address.

correct.explanation: The Interface field shows the local port receiving CDP (Gi0/2 on this switch) — it connects to the neighbor's Port ID (Gi0/1 on SwitchB).

incorrect.explanation: Holdtime (162 sec) is time remaining before the entry ages — not when the last advertisement was seen.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Reading holdtime as last-seen timestamp
incorrect.whatItDoes: The advertisement was seen 162 seconds ago. states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "neighbor", Switch B interface Gi0/2 connects to Switch A. satisfies what this question tests — The advertisement was seen 162 seconds ago. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Port ID lists the neighbor's outgoing interface (Gi0/1 on SwitchB) — the local Interface field is Gi0/2 facing SwitchB.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Swapping local Interface with neighbor Port ID
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch B interface Gi0/1 connects to Switch A. states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (neighbor): Switch B interface Gi0/2 connects to Switch A. matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — Switch B interface Gi0/1 connects to Switch A. breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: Entry address shows SwitchB management IP 192.168.1.2 — 192.168.1.1 is not listed in this CDP detail output.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Inventing neighbor IP not shown in CDP output
incorrect.whatItDoes: The IP address of Switch B is 192.168.1.1. shifts the answer to IP/Layer 3 addressing instead of Ethernet MAC learning.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: This is a Layer 2 process (neighbor). Switch B interface Gi0/2 connects to Switch A. uses Ethernet addresses — not IP headers.

answerReview.examTip: CDP detail: Interface = local port; Port ID = neighbor's port facing you.

questions.question: You have a layer 2 connection to your ISP. You want to make sure that you do not send information on the capabilities of your switch, but you don’t want to affect the use of CDP. Which command will you configure?
questions.explanation: no cdp enable disables CDP advertisements on one interface.

incorrect.explanation: cdp disable is not valid global syntax — per-interface suppression uses no cdp enable under the interface.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using invented cdp disable global command
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#cdp disable points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for no cdp enable disables CDP advertisements on one interface.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "no cdp enable disables CDP advertisements on one interface", Switch(config-if)#no cdp enable satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config)#cdp disable does not.

incorrect.explanation: no cdp is incomplete interface syntax — the command to stop CDP on one port is no cdp enable.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using no cdp instead of no cdp enable
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-if)#no cdp points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for no cdp enable disables CDP advertisements on one interface.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "no cdp enable disables CDP advertisements on one interface", Switch(config-if)#no cdp enable satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-if)#no cdp does not.

incorrect.explanation: no cdp disable would re-enable CDP if disable were set — it does not selectively stop advertisements to the ISP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Negating disable instead of disabling CDP on interface
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-if)#no cdp disable points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for no cdp enable disables CDP advertisements on one interface.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "no cdp enable disables CDP advertisements on one interface", Switch(config-if)#no cdp enable satisfies what this question tests — Switch(config-if)#no cdp disable does not.
